turns.text: Absolutely! In American culture, there's a phrase called "You don't say!" It's often used to express surprise or agreement, even when the statement being agreed upon isn't actually surprising. For example, if a friend says, "I've never been to Europe," and you respond with "You don't say!", you're not really commenting on the fact that the statement is surprising, but rather showing interest and encouraging your friend to share more about their travel plans. In this context, "You don't say!" serves as a casual way of saying, "Tell me more!" or "That's interesting!"
